Standing Tall When The Smoke Clears

precepts.why:
This is the Lord dealing with us as a nation. “Thou shalt remember all the way which the Lord thy God led thee these forty years in the wilderness, to humble thee, and to prove thee, to know what was in thine heart”. He led us in the wilderness forty years, going in circles, lacking bread and water at times, humbling us and proving us so he could see what was in our heart.

You can’t see what’s in a man’s or a woman’s heart when everything is good. You want to know if your wife is really down for you? Wait till y’all fall on hard times; you’ll find out what you married. That’s how you know what’s in somebody’s heart: when they are going through affliction. “Whether thou wouldest keep his commandments, or no.”

“And he humbled thee, and suffered thee to hunger, and fed thee with manna”, “that he might make thee know that man doth not live by bread only”. God wants us to show ourselves faithful whether we are going through prosperity or adversity, and to depend on him at all times, not trusting in uncertain riches or in this present life.

note.label: Standing Tall When The Smoke Clears

precepts.why:
That sister waited twelve years to be healed. Some of us are very impatient in this truth: we call for counsel on a Thursday and call again the same Thursday. You have to apply the understanding for a period of time before you double back.

“The Lord is good unto them that wait for him, to the soul that seeketh him.” You are not alone. Sometimes we think our prayers aren’t being heard. That’s not the case.

note.label: Standing Tall When The Smoke Clears

precepts.why:
Satan has you thinking you’re the only one going through it. Lies: we are all catching all manner of hell, and we are not alone. “They that trust in the Lord shall be as mount Zion, which cannot be removed, but abideth for ever.”

“As the mountains are round about Jerusalem, so the Lord is round about his people from henceforth even for ever.” We have to remember that. God has a purpose for everything: the pain, the trials, the suffering, the fiery furnace of affliction.

note.label: Standing Tall When The Smoke Clears

precepts.why:
“I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman.” “Every branch in me that beareth not fruit he taketh away”: some spirits have to be taken away.

“And every branch that beareth fruit”: that’s the sincere, those who apply with patience, “he purgeth it”. To purge a tree is to prune it: carefully cutting back branches to control its size and shape and to revitalise the plant. The plant has to lose parts of itself to be revitalised. To purge an area can also mean to root out weeds and unwanted plants encroaching on a garden; sometimes the Lord has to purge you to remove what’s around you that ain’t good for you. The word comes from the Latin meaning to cleanse.

“That it may bring forth more fruit.” He has to cut branches off of you so you grow in the right size and grow properly in the spirit, and that don’t feel good. If you are sincere, everything is to make you better. Pain, obstacles, struggles, correction, demotion: the sincere will come out the other side of whatever calamity they face wiser, stronger, with more fruits of the spirit, their senses exercised. You won’t be the same person that walked into the storm; you always gain something in spite of what you consider a loss.

points: A sower went out to sow his seed, the word of God, in us. Some fell by the wayside and was trodden down, and the fowls devoured it: Satan takes away the word that was planted.

note.label: A Tree Bearing No Fruits

points: Some fell upon a rock, sprang up, and withered away because it lacked moisture. That is the brother or sister who grows for a year or four years and then disappears, because there was no water, no word.

note.label: A Tree Bearing No Fruits

points: Some fell among thorns, and the thorns sprang up with it and choked it. As the word grows in you, sin, the cares of this world and the lust of the flesh grow alongside it, like weeds in a garden or Paul's thorn in the flesh. Cut the thorns out or they choke the word and you become unfruitful.

note.label: Luke 8: The Sower, the Storm, and the Works of Power

points: Christ “went throughout every city and village, preaching and shewing the glad tidings of the kingdom of God”. For the brothers teaching in the streets: ask trigger questions. Would you like to never have to work and never worry about your bills? To walk out of your house, sister, and know nobody is going to rape you, rob you or carjack you? To see your kids walk outside with no gunshots? To drive and not be afraid when you see a white police? They will keep saying yes; then show them how. That is fishing them in with the glad tidings: the kingdom of heaven is coming to you.

note.label: The War Between Blacks & Whites

points: “Certain women, which had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities, Mary called Magdalene, out of whom went seven devils”. She was healed.

note.label: The War Between Blacks & Whites

points: “And Joanna the wife of Chuza Herod’s steward, and Susanna, and many others, which ministered unto him of their substance.” The steward in Herod's own house: people working for Herod were repenting. You think he didn't see that? Susanna was right there, and now she has a head cover and is not eating pork.

There will be credible people among us, regular people holding jobs. Other camps will pull in brothers who still have the old mind, who want to rob and steal and stay drunk and commit adultery and don't want to reform; repentance is for them too, but those camps hit a ceiling. We are looking for people who want to change their lives. One day you will see somebody in the White House with fringes on, somebody in the mayor's office with a head covering, somebody in the FBI tucking their fringes in their suit. We are going to be everywhere.

note.label: The War Between Blacks & Whites

points: “A woman having an issue of blood twelve years”: a health problem she battled for twelve years. Imagine the pain and sorrow year after year, Passover after Passover, Tabernacles after Tabernacles, Atonement after Atonement: dang, Lord, I thought you forgave me. She “had spent all her living upon physicians”, so her health constraint became a financial constraint too, and she “neither could be healed of any”.

note.label: Standing Tall When The Smoke Clears

points: She “touched the border of his garment: and immediately her issue of blood stanched.” “Somebody hath touched me: for I perceive that virtue is gone out of me”: his power. When she saw she was not hid, she came trembling and declared before all the people why she had touched him, “and how she was healed immediately.”

note.label: Standing Tall When The Smoke Clears

points: “Daughter, be of good comfort: thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace.” Suffering will show your faith. When you endure your pain, your trial and your suffering, it shows the level of faith you have. God has a purpose behind every situation you might look at as inconvenient, and he deals with us individually and as a nation like that.

note.label: Standing Tall When The Smoke Clears

points: “But that on the good ground are they, which in an honest and good heart, having heard the word, keep it, and bring forth fruit with patience.” This is the sincere part of the body. Having heard the word, they keep it: that’s application.

And they bring forth fruit with patience. What do you need patience for? Because even when you are doing the right things, suffering is part of the walk, family. We are constantly growing, constantly learning, constantly being moulded in the potter’s hands into a better product.
